question: How should we add search to a small documentation site?
context: Synthetic experiment: a team has a static documentation site with about 200 public pages. The priority is useful search without taking on a new service.

options.title: Build a static search index
options.summary: Generate a compact index alongside the site and search it in the browser.
tradeoffs: Index size grows with the documentation

options.title: Use a hosted search service
options.summary: Send the public documentation to a managed search provider.
benefits: More capable ranking and search tooling
tradeoffs: Adds an external dependency and possible recurring cost
Requires reviewing provider privacy and indexing rules

options.title: Run our own search service
options.summary: Deploy a search backend with full control over indexing and querying.
benefits: Control over ranking, operations, and data
tradeoffs: More operational work than this site currently needs

recommendation.reason: For 200 public pages, a static index is the smallest operational commitment. Revisit hosted search if measured relevance or index size becomes a problem.
